Accident Claim Tribunal, Ranebennur, Partly Allowing The
 Claim Petition For Comepnsation And Seeking Enhancement
 Of Compensation.

This Mfa Coming On For Final Hearing This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant is impugning the judgment and award dated 02.12.2010 passed in MVC No.152 of 2009 on the file of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranibennur (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity), awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directing respondent No.1 to pay the same.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranibennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties are referred to as per their rank and status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, the claimant filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motors Vehicle's Act, 1988 (for short 'the MV Act'), against respondent No.1 - owner of Tata Ace bearing registration No.KA-27/A-435 and respondent No.2 - insurer for the injuries suffered by him in the road traffic accident.
It is contended that the petitioner is a Government servant earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
On 25.03.2008 at 5.30 p.m. he was proceeding on PB road and the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle came in a rash and negligent NC: 2023:KHC-D:7357 manner and dashed against the petitioner

, as a result, the petitioner sustained multiple fractures and took treatment with Dr.Umanath R Ullal Hospital, Ranibennur and again at Kasturba Hospital and spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

Therefore, he claimed compensation from respondent Nos.1 and 2.
4.
The claim of the claimant was resisted by respondent No.2 by filing objections denying the contention taken by the claimant.
It is stated that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective licence.
Hence, he is not liable for compensation.
Accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of these pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:
"1.
Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries in the said accident in RTA as contended in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?"

2 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7357 6.
The claimant examined himself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P20 in support of his contention.
Respondent No.2 examined RW1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R3 in support of his defence.

The Tribunal after taking into consideration all the materials on record answered issue Nos.1 and 2 in the affirmative and held that the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from respondent No.1, while dismissing the claim petition against respondent No.2.
7.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant is before this Court.
8. Heard Sri Vishwanath L Hedge, learned counsel for the appellant.
Learned counsel for the respondent is absent.
He has not addressed his arguments in spite of giving sufficient opportunity.
Hence, his arguments is taken as NIL.
Perused the materials including the Trial Court records.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the claimant is aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
The claimant has sustained three fractures and was hospitalized for a period of 37 days.
He has NC: 2023:KHC-D:7357 spent more than Rs.88,000/- for his treatment in spite of that, the amount awarded is only Rs.50,000/-.
Therefore, he prays for allowing the appeal.

10. In view of the contentions of the learned counsel for the appellant, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal suffers from any infirmity and calls for interference by this Court?"

My answer to the above point is in the 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 11.
The only contention raised by the claimant is with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

The materials placed before the Court discloses that the claimant met with an accident on 25.03.2008 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata Ace bearing registration No.KA-27/A-435.
Ex.P5 is the wound certificate according to which, the claimant sustained multiple injuries.

He sustained fracture of both bones of right fore arm and bones NC:
2023:KHC-D:7357 were displaced, injuries on the left side of the chest and fracture of 5th and 6th ribs on the right side and injuries to pelvic bone and fracture of interior armor of right pubic bones.
12. Ex.P8 is the medical certificate to the effect that the claimant was admitted to the hospital and treated as inpatient from 25.03.2008 till 17.04.2008.

Ex.P13 is the discharge card issued by the Kasturba Hospital, according to which, he admitted to the hospital on 11.01.2009 and discharged on 13.01.2009 and again he was admitted at Kastubra Hospital on 28.01.2009 and discharged on 10.02.2009.
During this period, he was operated for fixation of implants.

Thus, the claimant was Basavaraja S/O Kotrappa Nalavagal vs Vivekananada S/O Vinayaka Raikar on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45805850/
3 treated as inpatient for about 37 days.

sentences.text: 13. Since the claimant has suffered three fractures as per the wound certificate which is also supported by discharge card, claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Since he was taken treatment as inpatient for a period of 37 days, he is entitled for compensation towards hospitalization, conveyance and attendant charges at Rs.50,000/-.

The claimant has also produced Ex.P15 to 20 - the medical bills and report, according to which,
he has spent Rs.88,671/-.
Looking to the nature of injuries, duration of treatment and the medical bills produced by the claimant, I am of the opinion that the claimant is entitled for the said amount.
Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the claimant has not claimed reimbursement in his department towards the medical expenses and the original documents are produced before the Court.
Accepting the said submission, I am of the opinion that the claimant is entitled for compensation towards medical expenses at Rs.88,671/-.
The claimant is working as Government servant and he continued to be in service.
He has not suffered any permanent disability.
15. Under such circumstances, the claimant is entitled for the following:.
Sl. Awarded by this  Particulars No. Court in Rs.

1 Pain and suffering 50,000/-
2

Towards hospitalization, 50,000/-
 conveyance and attendant charges 3

Towards medical expenses 88,671/-
 TOTAL 1,88,671/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7357 16.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of only Rs.50,000/-.
It has not taken into consideration the medical expenses incurred by the claimant nor it has considered the hospitalization of the claimant for more than a month.
Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for interference.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed with costs.

4 (ii) The judgment and award dated 02.12.2010 passed in MVC No.152 of 2009 on the file of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranibennur, is hereby modified.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranibennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (iii) The appellant-claimant is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,88,671/- rounded off to Rs.1,88,670/- as against Rs.50,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal.
Remaining order of the Tribunal remains intact.
Registry is directed to draw the award accordingly.
Registry is also directed to send back the Trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment and award.

SD/-
